lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: health and safety support

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic health and safety support task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Rather than looking up any real person's information, the learner labels three generic support roles for the persona's plan (a doctor, a pharmacy, and one trusted adult contact) and describes in one sentence each what role that contact plays, then picks one plausible emergency scenario that could happen during the persona's invented month (such as a minor injury at work or feeling seriously ill on a day off) and writes the specific first step the persona should take.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which of the three roles would be hardest for your persona to reach quickly in the scenario you chose, and what does that suggest about a backup option?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears. | Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a second plausible emergency scenario of a different type (physical versus safety-related) and write its own first step and role match, comparing how the two responses differ.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic health and safety support task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: health and safety support worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Rather than looking up any real person's information, the learner labels three generic support roles for the persona's plan (a doctor, a pharmacy, and one trusted adult contact) and describes in one sentence each what role that contact plays, then picks one plausible emergency scenario that could happen during the persona's invented month (such as a minor injury at work or feeling seriously ill on a day off) and writes the specific first step the persona should take.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact health and safety support decision or action.
Model move 2: Before writing the plan, think through why each role matters.
Model move 3: Fill in the generic support-contact plan using role labels only - never a real name, address, or phone number.

Model check: Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears. | Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role.

resources.title: health and safety support action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for health and safety support.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: health and safety support coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Rather than looking up any real person's information, the learner labels three generic support roles for the persona's plan (a doctor, a pharmacy, and one trusted adult contact) and describes in one sentence each what role that contact plays, then picks one plausible emergency scenario that could happen during the persona's invented month (such as a minor injury at work or feeling seriously ill on a day off) and writes the specific first step the persona should take.
Coach direction: Before writing the plan, think through why each role matters.
Learner prompt: In one sentence each, explain why a doctor, a pharmacy, and one trusted adult contact are each useful roles for someone living independently to have identified in advance.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: health and safety support complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Fill in the generic support-contact plan using role labels only - never a real name, address, or phone number.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I labeled a doctor role and wrote one sentence describing what the persona would contact this role for.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I labeled a pharmacy role and wrote one sentence describing what the persona would contact this role for.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I labeled one trusted adult contact role and wrote one sentence describing what makes someone trustworthy enough for this role.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: health and safety support minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which of the three roles would be hardest for your persona to reach quickly in the scenario you chose, and what does that suggest about a backup option?

Success checks: Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears. | Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: health and safety support supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional health and safety support condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears. | Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: health and safety support — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the health and safety support task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which of the three roles would be hardest for your persona to reach quickly in the scenario you chose, and what does that suggest about a backup option?
observableCriteria: Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears.
Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Support-role plan completeness and genericness: All three roles are labeled generically with a clear one-sentence purpose for each, and no real identifying information appears. | Emergency-response reasoning: A plausible scenario is named, paired with a specific first step and a matching support role.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u06-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
